sections.h2: Start with the fire prevention certificate
sections.html:
Raritan will not let a house close without a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate from the borough fire prevention office. Book it the week you sign a contract, because everything else on your closing calendar waits on it. The same office also inspects rentals, so a house with a tenant adds a second set of paperwork.

Raritan is a small Somerset County borough on the Raritan River. It had 7,835 residents in 2020 and an estimated 8,516 in July 2025, an increase of 8.7 percent. The borough covers only 1.99 square miles of land, so lots are small and buyers judge a house that needs work against the neighbors within a block or two. About half of households own their home (49.9 percent), which means plenty of landlords and tenant-occupied sales.

Rents are well above the national figure and the typical owner-occupied home is worth more than the national midpoint, so a repaired house has a real market here.

The borough has 3,326 households averaging 2.50 people. About 42.7 percent of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home, so listing material and disclosure forms often need to reach buyers in more than one language.

sections.h2: What the fire prevention office checks
sections.html:
The borough fire prevention office handles smoke detector certification for the sale of dwellings. Older homes with battery detectors need one on every occupied level. Homes with hard-wired interconnected detectors must have every unit sound together when one is tested.

  • A carbon monoxide detector must be mounted within 10 feet of every sleeping area, and a house with bedrooms on more than one level needs more than one.
  • Fire detection systems must be inspected every year under state rules, so a house with a monitored alarm needs its alarm company or an electrician to put the system on test during the visit.
  • New Jersey dropped the portable fire extinguisher from resale inspections effective February 3, 2025. Ask the office which items it checks before you buy one.

Fire code violations in Raritan have no statute of limitations, so one that turns up late must still be corrected. Talk to the office before you pick a closing date. If a device fails, replace it and rebook promptly.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or two-family house
sections.html:
The Property Maintenance office keeps the register of rental properties and inspects each rental unit before it is reoccupied. Own a duplex or a house with a renter? The buyer's attorney will want proof that the unit sits on the register and passed its inspection.

The same office responds to complaints about upkeep on residential and commercial buildings and enforces the rules for putting out trash, recycling and bulk items. A complaint still open against your address can hold up the closing. Phone the office and find out if one exists.

Before you call, collect the rental registration, the date of the last inspection, the names on the lease and any notice the borough sent about the building. One folder with all of it lets your attorney answer a buyer in a single reply.

sections.h2: How do I appeal my Raritan assessment?
sections.html:
Somerset County sets April 1, 4:30 p.m., as the deadline for an assessment appeal from Raritan to reach the county tax board. File a paper petition with the fee, by mail or at the office, and send copies to the municipal assessor and the municipal clerk.

The thing you contest is the assessed value. The board starts from the assumption that the assessment is right. Your job is to show otherwise with comparable sales from the year before the October 1 assessment date. Taxes and charges also have to be current through February 1 of the hearing year, or the board can throw the appeal out.

The Somerset County Tax Board is at 27 Warren Street, fourth floor, Somerville, and its number is 908-541-5701. An added assessment appeal, for new construction picked up mid-year, has a December 1 deadline.

New Jersey charges the seller a Realty Transfer Fee, collected as the deed goes on record. Each band of the state schedule applies only to the part of the price inside that band, so the bill climbs with the sale price. Ask your attorney or title agent for the exact number before closing day.

A landlord who lives outside New Jersey fills out a GIT/REP-1 at the closing table unless a seller assurance covers the sale. The prepayment is the gain times 10.75 percent, with a floor of 2 percent of the deed price. Residents of the state sign the GIT/REP-3. If a county clerk refuses a deed, go back to that clerk, then to the state GIT/REP unit at 609-322-9275.

sections.h2: What to have ready for the closing attorney
sections.html:
A complete file on day one shortens a Raritan closing. Gather these before you sign.

  • The fire prevention certificate, or the appointment date if the visit has not happened yet.
  • For a rental, the borough registration and proof of the last unit inspection.
  • Any permits for work done on the house, with the final sign-off.
  • Your current tax bill, and a note of whether taxes are paid through the quarter due.
  • Your residency status for the GIT/REP form, since an owner who lives out of state follows a different path from a New Jersey resident.

Cash buyers move as fast as the paperwork does. Mortgage buyers add an appraisal and underwriting, and an unclosed permit or missing detector tends to stall there.

sections.h2: How a cash sale changes the Raritan steps
sections.html:
An as-is cash offer removes the lender's appraisal and repair list. It does not remove the borough's certificate, and the seller normally still arranges it.

The order is short: contract, call to the fire prevention office that day, repairs to any missing detector, passed visit, certificate to the attorney. With a tenant in place, raise the rental registration with Property Maintenance in the same week.

faqs.q: Does Raritan require a certificate of occupancy to sell a house?
faqs.a: The borough fire prevention office certifies smoke detectors for the sale of dwellings, and that is the document you need. Ask the borough whether any other resale paperwork applies to your address.

faqs.q: What smoke alarm rules apply to a Raritan sale?
faqs.a: Every occupied level needs a working smoke detector, and hard-wired interconnected units must all sound together. Carbon monoxide detectors go within 10 feet of each sleeping area. The state removed the fire extinguisher item from resale inspections on February 3, 2025.

faqs.q: When is the Raritan appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 at 4:30 p.m. Hearings come later in the year. Added assessment appeals are due December 1.
The borough's Property Maintenance office. It keeps the rental register and inspects each unit before it is reoccupied, so a seller with a tenant should confirm the unit is on the register.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee on a Raritan sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it when the deed is recorded with the county clerk. The amount rises with the price, and your closing attorney can quote it.
